question: In which amongst the following acts was Delhi declared the capital of British India in place of Calcutta?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Morley - Minto Act, 1909**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Morley - Minto Act, 1909** declared Delhi as the capital of British India, replacing Calcutta.
 
• This act is also known as the **Indian Councils Act 1909**.
 
• The decision to shift the capital was announced by **King George V** during the **Delhi Durbar** in December 1911.
 
• The shift was officially implemented in 1912.
 
• The move aimed to have a more centrally located capital and to placate the growing political unrest in Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Government of India Act, 1858** marked the end of the East India Company's rule in India and transferred control to the British Crown.
 
• The **Government of India Act, 1935** provided for provincial autonomy and the establishment of a federal government in India.
 
• The **Montagu Chelmsford Act, 1919**, also known as the Government of India Act 1919, introduced a dual system of governance (dyarchy) in the provinces.
 
• Delhi was chosen for its strategic location and historical significance as a seat of power in India.
 
• The shift of the capital was a significant event in the history of British India, symbolizing administrative and political changes.
